name: unshare
description: Runs a program with selected kernel namespaces unshared from the parent — the primitive behind containers.

flags.description: New mount namespace — mounts inside do not affect the host.
New network namespace (own interfaces, own loopback).
Map your user to root inside the namespace (user namespaces).

examples.explanation: A shell in its own mount namespace: mounts made inside vanish when it exits — try mounting a tmpfs to see the isolation.
A shell with a private, empty network stack: only a down loopback. The basis of container networking.
Private PID space with its own /proc — inside, your shell is PID 1.

about: Linux namespaces partition kernel resources: mount, PID, network, UTS (hostname), IPC, user, cgroup. Containers (Docker, podman) are namespaces + cgroups + union filesystems. unshare lets you experiment with these primitives directly — the best way to understand what a container actually is.
mistakes: Expecting full isolation from one namespace flag — each namespace isolates only its own resource type.
warnings: User namespaces expand the kernel attack surface; hardened systems restrict them (kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone).
